Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As Compute & Infrastructure Counsel, Real Estate at Anthropic, you'll drive legal execution for Anthropic's largest physical infrastructure transactions: direct datacenter leases, construction agreements, and the financing structures that enable infrastructure investments at massive scale. This role focuses on facilities where Anthropic has direct control through ownership or long-term lease, complementing the colo & networks, and cloud compute legal teammates (facilities where Anthropic is tenant, and our hyperscaler relationships, respectively). You'll work in close partnership with specialized outside counsel on financing and real estate matters, serving as the in-house coordinator who ensures external work product aligns with Anthropic's commercial objectives and integrates with our overall compute strategy. Responsibilities Negotiate long-term datacenter leases with major developers, and represent some of Anthropic's largest and lengthiest capital commitments Coordinate construction-adjacent agreements including design-build contracts, equipment procurement, and commissioning schedules Manage legal workstreams for complex financing structures (e.g., sale-leasebacks, tax components, or project finance vehicles) Work closely with specialized outside counsel (real estate and financing specialists), ensuring their work product aligns with Anthropic's commercial objectives Collaborate with compute team's transaction managers who handle operational execution and project management, providing legal and risk management expertise Coordinate with finance and corporate development on strategic deal structuring Understand how datacenter legal structures interact with the compute capacity they will house e.g., power requirements, cooling specifications, security standards, and expansion rights all flow from decisions made elsewhere in the Compute organization Escalate novel structures or terms that create downstream risk for Anthropic's operational flexibility to managers; ensure facility designs accommodate AI-specific requirements including high-density power, liquid cooling infrastructure, and rapid scaling capacity Minimum qualifications JD and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar Fluency in commercial real estate and construction contracting; datacenter lease structures, construction risk allocation, and financing arrangements (and how they will interact) Experience with EPC, AIA, and design-build arrangements at scale Comfort with project finance structures and the interplay between lease, financing, and development agreements Ability to coordinate effectively with specialized outside counsel while maintaining strategic direction Strong judgment about when deal terms create downstream risk for operational flexibility Effective collaboration skills for working with business teams who handle transaction management and site selection Communication skills that translate complex real estate and financing concepts into clear risk assessments for business stakeholders Genuine interest in infrastructure development and appreciation for why datacenter capacity is mission-critical for frontier AI Preferred qualifications At least 8 years of relevant legal experience with meaningful exposure to infrastructure real estate transactions, project finance, or construction contracts In-house experience at datacenter developers supporting leasing, project development, and financing transactions Background at infrastructure private equity firms with exposure to datacenter or similar infrastructure investments Experience at large technology companies with datacenter construction programs supporting development transactions from the buy side Law firm experience at practices with infrastructure finance or project development specialization, particularly those who have worked on datacenter, power, or similar infrastructure financings Prior involvement in transactions requiring sophisticated understanding of construction timelines, commissioning requirements, and operational handoff Familiarity with tax structures, sale-leaseback arrangements, or other financing vehicles used in large-scale infrastructure development Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or Seattle office at least 3 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $335,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Model Policy Manager, Multimodal Safety
items.description: About the Team Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models, ensuring our models are deployed responsibly and have a positive impact on society. Our work spans diverse research and engineering initiatives—from system-level safeguards and model training to evaluation and red-teaming—all aimed at mitigating misuse, misalignment, and maintaining our high bar for safety. We lead OpenAI's commitment to developing and deploying safe Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), fostering a culture of trust, responsibility, and transparency. Our goal is to continuously learn from deployments, distribute AI’s benefits widely, and ensure that powerful tools remain aligned with human values and safety considerations. Within Safety Systems, the Model Policy team works to ensure that frontier models behave safely and reliably in real-world environments by designing policies that define safe model behavior. Our relevant publications include: - Safety at every step https://openai.com/safety/ - OpenAI GPT6 System Card https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-6-astra - OpenAI Model Spec https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-model-spec/ - GPT-Live https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/ - ChatGPT Images 2.5 https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/ About the Role We are hiring a Model Policy Manager to focus on the safety of multimodal models. In this role, you will shape how OpenAI identifies, evaluates, and addresses risks in multimodal AI models - such as GPT-Live https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/ and ChatGPT Images https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-0/ - as well as multimodal capabilities in frontier AI models. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Design and maintain model policies for audio, image, video, and omni-modal behavior. - Translate theories of harm and threat models into behavioral safety policies, evaluation criteria, grading guidance, and safeguards. - Identify and analyze safety regressions and failure patterns to identify gaps in existing policies and inform policy iteration. - Develop policy artifacts that support model training, evaluation, and deployment, including behavior instructions, human-data campaigns, golden sets, and evaluations. - Partner with AI researchers, domain experts, and product teams to operationalize policy into measurable model behavior. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have strong judgment about the real-world risks of advanced multimodal AI systems. - Possess experience turning ambiguous safety questions into clear data-driven policies, behavioral boundaries, and measurable evaluation criteria. - Treat policy as an end-to-end, measurable system by testing whether it produces the intended model behavior and diagnosing gaps across policy, data, graders, and safeguards. - Leverage strong technical judgement to design policies around model behavior that can realistically be trained, measured, and supervised at scale. - Demonstrate strong technical fluency and uses AI tools to accelerate policy development, evaluate model behavior, analyze failure patterns, and turn findings into actionable improvements. - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures. - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change. - Take a pragmatic, evidence-driven approach to reducing risk while preserving beneficial uses of AI. - Have hands-on experience driving consensus and action in ambiguous spaces. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy https://cdn.openai.com/policies/global-employee-and-contractor-privacy-policy.pdf At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

items.title: Customer Success Manager, Public Sector (National Security)
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Customer Success Manager on Anthropic's Public Sector team, you will be the post-sales trusted advisor helping national security customers realize the value of Claude and turn their investment into mission impact. You'll combine your customer success expertise with technical fluency to drive adoption of Claude Code, the Claude API, and Claude for Government (C4G) on classified infrastructure delivered through a cleared cloud provider, while maintaining our high standards for safety, security, and discretion. Working closely with our Sales, Applied AI, Product, Engineering, and Policy teams, you'll guide customers from deployment through enablement, model migration, renewal, and expansion. You'll develop genuine partnerships with customers' AI leadership, platform and compute teams, security and accreditation officials, and mission operators—and with the cleared cloud providers and system integrators that deliver alongside us. Your understanding of their mission, how they accredit and govern capabilities on classified fabrics, and how they evidence value to oversight will help them deliver decision advantage. Drawing on both your national security expertise and technical knowledge, you'll serve as a strategic advisor throughout their journey with us—helping them navigate constraints that don't exist in commercial or federal civilian deployments: classified-fabric accreditation, fixed compute capacity, compartmentation, limited telemetry, and need-to-know discipline. Much of this work happens onsite, in the customer's spaces, on their systems. Your role focuses on driving consumption and adoption of Claude across mission workloads, standing up enablement and change management suited to a cleared, mission-driven workforce, identifying and hardening the workloads that matter most to the mission, and demonstrating value in unclassified terms that can leave the building and support renewal and expansion. The insights you gather will directly inform our research priorities, product roadmap, and national security strategy—making you a key voice in shaping how Anthropic builds and delivers AI systems for the most demanding missions. Key responsibilities: Partner with the account executive and Applied AI architect to deeply understand the customer's mission requirements and translate them into an account and success plan, ensuring alignment between mission objectives, the customer's investment, and technical implementation Serve as the primary post-sales advisor to the customer throughout their Claude adoption journey, from deployment through enablement, model migration, renewal, and expansion. You will need to build trusted relationships across the customer's senior stakeholders—AI leadership, platform and compute teams, security and accreditation officials, contracting, and mission operators—and coordinate internally across multiple teams and with cleared cloud providers to drive customer success Support customers building with Claude Code, the Claude API, and Claude for Government on classified infrastructure—managed configuration, capacity and throughput planning, and workload onboarding—with a working understanding of accreditation requirements (FedRAMP High, IL5/IL6, classified-fabric accreditation) Create and deliver compelling enablement and executive content tailored to different audiences. You will need to spread the gamut from hands-on Claude Code enablement for engineering teams (Train the Trainer, managed configuration as the "paved road," Center of Excellence development) up to mission-value conversations with senior agency leadership, in unclassified language that can leave the building Help the customer develop evaluation frameworks and measure adoption and value without direct telemetry—provider capacity reports, customer-run dashboards, workload registries, and agreed leading indicators—and guide model migration and release readiness: eval gates built from their workloads, staged cutovers off end-of-support models, and realistic expectations about what lands on their fabric and when Drive consumption and adoption: separate under-pacing from burst saturation of a fixed compute pool, smooth and onboard workloads before asking for capacity, discover new mission workloads across compartmented organizations, and document value realized in mission-outcome terms (decisions accelerated, coverage, timeliness, findings produced) Own Executive Business Reviews that function as discovery and alignment—leaving executives with sponsor commitments, mutual next steps, and a mission-outcome narrative that supports the renewal decision—and serve as the primary conduit between the customer, cleared cloud providers, and Anthropic Identify common adoption and integration patterns and hero workflows that demonstrate mission transformation, and contribute insights back to our Product, Engineering, Research, and Policy teams—while maintaining strict separation of classified and unclassified channels and escalating correctly (e.g., 'Claude cut a high-volume analytic triage queue from days to hours') Work onsite frequently at customer facilities for enablement, workshops, and relationship building, on the customer’s systems and within their security and need-to-know rules Maintain strong knowledge of the latest developments in LLM capabilities, agentic and Claude Code implementation patterns, and national security AI policy You may be a good fit if you have: Due to U.S. Government contract requirements, this position requires U.S. citizenship and an active TS/SCI security clearance with a current full-scope polygraph (a TS/SCI with CI polygraph may be considered where crossover is supportable) Must have prior experience working with US national security (defense and/or intelligence) agencies —ideally at the level of AI leadership, platform, and compute teams rather than a single program office—and a working knowledge of how national security agencies accredit, budget, govern compute, and measure mission (including the difference between FedRAMP High, IL5/IL6, and classified-fabric accreditation, and the role of cleared cloud providers and system integrators) 5+ years of experience in customer-facing roles such as Customer Success Manager, Technical Account Manager, Solutions Architect, or Consultant, with items.title: Executive Producer, Executive Communications
items.description: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? Cohere has a strong AI narrative, the most deployable product, and a CEO who co-authored the foundational paper of modern AI. The company is positioned to become the transatlantic leader in sovereign AI for enterprise and government, and needs a storytelling engine to deliver that story at scale. This role sits within the team that is building that engine. We're looking for an Executive Producer, Executive Communications to own and evolve Cohere’s narrative globally as we grow to become the transatlantic leader in sovereign AI. This is a rare opportunity to use video as the primary medium to share voices and tell stories of executives at one of the fastest growing companies in the most dynamic space in technology. In this cross functional role, you will partner directly with C-Suite and VP executives, helping to determine how we talk to customers, partners, and employees. The role takes Cohere's narrative—the through-line that connects sovereign AI, transatlantic growth, and the product story—and turns it into the content the world sees and shares. You will execute Cohere's strategic narrative through various forms of content including video, podcast, and in-house production. While the role flexes across formats, we see video as the primary and most effective medium. The Executive Producer has dual aims: to grow the personal thought leadership profiles of Cohere's senior voices on their own channels and to deliver Cohere's narrative to the market through company channels. As Executive Producer, Executive Communications you will: - Build and execute Cohere's strategic narrative across three storytelling surfaces: Executive Thought Leadership, Policy Storytelling, and Corporate Storytelling - Partner with the VP Global Communications on narrative architecture and translating Cohere's narrative into content strategy and execution across the aforementioned three storytelling surfaces - Audit and gap analyses across Cohere's senior voices including the co-founding team, CFO, Chief AI Officer, SVP Government Affairs, and various VPs supporting the business - Develop content playbooks for predictable inflection moments (regulatory milestones, product launches, customer wins, IPO milestones) to be launched on executive and company pages - Partner with Marketing to create content for company accounts - Stand up the production function including stage capture systems, content atomization workflows, and freelance crew networks - Build AI-enabled workflows using Cohere's own products (Command, North, Embed, Rerank) for transcript-to-asset pipelines, executive prep automation, and narrative consistency - Initiate executive stage content capture and distribution at major events with lean, scalable production - Conduct executive content audits and gap analyses across senior voices - Refine and systematize content production workflows with predictable cadences - Develop flagship thought leadership pieces and corporate storytelling output - Scale successful surfaces based on impact analysis and team capacity You may be a good fit if you: - Have 8-10 years of experience building executive and corporate narratives from ideation through execution, ideally within a fast-paced, high-growth tech or AI environment - Are adept are creating production workflows from scratch (stage capture systems, content atomization pipelines) - Have experience in the high-paced broadcast television environment - Have experience building trust and rapport with executives and senior leaders naturally - Are scrappy. You thrive in thinking “outside the box” and find joy in marrying a problem to its solution - Are highly organized and process-driven, with strong project management skills and a bias for action - Bring high levels of creativity to communications – in format, channel, and storytelling - Are comfortable navigating organizational dynamics and building strong relationships across all levels - Thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and know how to ruthlessly prioritize Ideal Candidate Profile The successful candidate will have experience in strategic communications, content production, and executive storytelling, with the ability to build scalable systems and leverage AI tools. They should be comfortable navigating executive relationships, managing production workflows, and adapting content strategies based on performance data. Experience in tech/AI environments and familiarity with Cohere's product suite would be valuable assets. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Product Engagement Specialist on the User Operations team you will be a hands-on systems builder responsible for making product launches and frontline feedback more scaleable, measurable and actionable across both internal User Operations and external third-party teams. You’ll be responsible for not only managing the project timelines, but also designing and shipping the workflows, tooling and data systems that connect the voice of the user into actionable improvements for Product and Engineering teams. We’re looking for people who thrive at the intersection of project management, team enablement, and customer advocacy, and enjoy working cross-functionally in a fast-paced, evolving environment. We are also looking for individuals that will not just do the day to day work - but will also be deeply involved in architecting the systems of feedback sharing and collection with our stakeholder groups across Support, Product, and Engineering. Think data systems, not better slide decks. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Design, build, and own scalable systems for launch readiness, feedback capture, triage, synthesis, and routing. - Coordinate product launches across internal User Operations teams and external third party teams to ensure seamless execution and support readiness. - Develop and implement scalable feedback loops between support teams and product/engineering teams, ensuring customer insights are integrated into product development and strategy. - Serve as the voice of the user, advocating for their needs and pain points in product and engineering discussions. - Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g., Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Operations) to align on product launch goals and timelines. - Lead efforts to document and standardize launch procedures, ensuring they are easily repeatable and scalable as the product line grows. - Monitor post-launch performance, gathering data from support teams to evaluate product impact and inform future improvements. - Identify potential risks and challenges during product rollouts, proposing solutions to mitigate disruptions to customer service. - Regularly report on the performance of the feedback loop, including key insights, trends, and actionable recommendations for the product roadmap. items.title: Consumer Support Specialist
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Support team at Perplexity AI is the frontline of our user experience. We ensure that our AI-powered search and answer engine delivers real value to every user—from individual consumers to teams and organizations. Our team operates across 3-4 active support channels—email, in-app messaging, Slack, and community—and collaborates closely with Product, Engineering, Billing, and Growth to turn user feedback into product improvements. We’re a lean, fast-moving group at a startup that ships constantly, so everyone on the team wears multiple hats and contributes well beyond just resolving tickets. ABOUT THE ROLE Perplexity launches new features and products at a rapid pace—and this role sits at the center of that. We need a Consumer Support Specialist who combines excellent customer support instincts with real technical depth. You’ll handle high volumes of user inquiries across channels while also digging into product issues, using customer feedback to uncover problems, and providing solutions that improve the experience for everyone. This isn’t just ticket work. As new features and products ship, you’re the person who hears about it first from users—what’s working, what’s confusing, and what’s broken. You’ll use those interactions to surface insights that shape how launches land, identify issues before they scale, and provide clear solutions back to users. You’ll also build automations and improve workflows that make the team faster and smarter, so we can keep up with the pace of the product without sacrificing quality. You should be comfortable operating across multiple support channels and have experience standing up or optimizing multi-channel support operations—not just working in them, but thinking critically about how they’re structured, routed, and scaled. This role requires someone who can navigate ambiguity and fill in the gaps where processes don’t yet exist. You won’t always have a playbook—and that’s the point. We need someone who can define the path forward, not just follow one. You’re a strong, independent operator who doesn’t need to be told what to do next: - You see the gap—whether it’s a missing Help Center article, a broken workflow, or a pattern in user tickets—and you move to fix it - You’re self-motivated and take initiative, but you also know when to ask questions - You communicate effectively with the team—keeping people informed, surfacing blockers early, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks - We won’t hold your hand through this role, and we wouldn’t want to—because you’re the kind of person who thrives when given ownership and trust RESPONSIBILITIES - Handle a high volume of user inquiries across channels (email, chat, Slack, community) with speed, accuracy, and empathy for both consumer and business users. - Deliver excellent customer support—clear, thoughtful, and human—even under pressure and at scale - Triage and prioritize effectively to keep response and resolution times on target - Use customer feedback and support interactions as a primary source for uncovering product issues, UX confusion, and feature gaps—especially as new products and features launch - Investigate and troubleshoot product issues: reproduce problems, isolate root causes, provide users with solutions or workarounds, and document findings for Engineering - Guide users through technical troubleshooting: AI search, LLM behavior, account configuration - File well-documented bugs in Linear with enough context for Engineering to act immediately - Leverage AI tooling and automation (Intercom, scripts) to streamline operations, reduce repetitive work, and scale support quality - Write and maintain Help Center articles, internal SOPs, escalation playbooks, and troubleshooting guides - Communicate cross-functionally—surface user insights to Product and Engineering, escalate issues, close the loop, and keep teammates informed - Track support KPIs and propose data-driven process improvements REQUIREMENTS - 3+ years in customer support, user operations, or technical support—ideally at a SaaS or tech company - Proven ability to manage high ticket volumes while maintaining quality and empathy - Excellent customer-facing communication: clear, professional, and adaptable to different audiences - Technical aptitude: comfortable working through product issues, navigating technical questions independently, and learning new tools and systems quickly - Hands-on experience with AI tools and automation platforms (Intercom workflows, scripting) to improve operations - Familiarity with AI, LLMs, or search technologies - Strong internal communication—keeps their immediate team informed, writes crisp updates for immediate team and cross-functional partners (Product, Engineering, etc.), and ensures stakeholders stay in the loop on issues and progress - Self-motivated and proactive: manages own priorities, takes initiative, delivers without waiting for direction - Experience creating user-facing documentation (e.g., Help Center articles, FAQs, guides) as well as internal SOPs, templates, and playbooks - items.title: Product Manager, Safe Access
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As Claude reaches more people, including individuals, businesses, developers building on our APIs, and the platforms and resellers building on top of those, knowing who is on the other side of a request and what they are allowed to do becomes foundational to running our products responsibly. Creating a centralized identity, verification, and access system that every Claude surface draws on is important to accomplishing our mission. We are hiring a Product Manager to own the safe access. The primitives are the building blocks the rest of Anthropic uses to manage access to models and capabilities: access programs, accounts, organization linking, verifications, user APIs for platforms, and the internal tooling teams use. You will own the end-to-end product experience and strategy for internal and external access,, across every surface. This is a role for a strong executor with the ability to be agile in shipping in a 0-1 product space. Safe access is a new product that sits on the critical path of every model launch and every access program. Requirements arrive from many organizations at once, and most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it. Key responsibilities Own the product strategy and roadmap for the account and access primitives, with the goal that any team at Anthropic can provision access or run an access program with minimal support. This is highly ambiguous and requires a lot of cross team coordination and deep understanding of the systems of today. Own the end-to-end experience of getting and managing access for internal stakeholders (research, model launches, safeguards, go-to-market) and for external customers and partners, and keep it consistent across every surface. This requires thinking through many user types, with vastly different experiences. Support the API designs and the UX of the access APIs that platforms, resellers, and internal services integrate with. Work through the designs with engineering and make calls on the primitives yourself. Partner with the trusted access and verification product managers so that new programs compose from shared primitives rather than one-off builds. Coordinate across the product, safeguards, legal, and go-to-market teams, and drive alignment when their requirements conflict. Minimum qualifications Are a strong executor with a track record of shipping through ambiguity and cross-organization dependencies. Write clearly enough that an engineer, an executive, and an external partner can each see the tradeoff you are making. Have owned a developer platform, identity, authorization, or access-management product end to end, and were the person accountable for its outcomes (for most people this means five or more years as a PM, but we care about the ownership, not the years). Care about Anthropic's mission, and specifically about scaling access to Claude safely. Preferred qualifications 8+ years of product management experience Experience with multi-tenant platforms consumed by first-party apps, direct API customers, and third parties building on top Built account, identity, or subscription systems that span more than one product Taken a product from zero to one, where the users, the product, and the requirements all had to be worked out at once The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $305,000 — $385,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As a member of the US Talent Acquisition team focused on Research and technical hiring, you will be instrumental in building and scaling Mistral's US-based research and engineering teams from the ground up. Joining early means you'll help shape both our technical recruitment strategy and operations, partnering closely with Research leadership across Research Science, Research Engineering, and adjacent technical functions. Your work will directly influence Mistral's frontier-model ambitions by ensuring we find and engage exceptional researchers and engineers who will drive Mistral's growth in the US. In this role, you'll also foster a strong candidate experience and help establish technical recruiting best practices as we expand across the US. What You Will Do Technical Stakeholder Partnership - Partner deeply with technical leaders — from Research Scientists and Research Engineers to team leads and hiring managers — to understand hiring needs, define role specs, and identify the right technical talent - Own full-cycle recruitment across Research Science and Research Engineering, with flexibility to support other technical roles as they come along - Advise hiring managers on market mapping, leveling, comp positioning, and the competitive landscape for US research and engineering talent - Translate the nuances of each technical role into compelling, accurate candidate outreach End-to-End Technical Recruitment - Own the full recruiting lifecycle from sourcing to close, operating with autonomy on complex, competitive technical roles - Source passive and active candidates across US research and engineering talent pools — from PhD students and postdocs to experienced researchers and engineers at leading AI labs, universities, and technology companies - Conduct intake and calibration sessions with hiring managers to align on ideal candidate profiles and stage expectations - Drive efficient, high-conversion pipelines and close candidates in a fiercely competitive market for top research talent Candidate Experience & Selling Mistral - Guide candidates through the hiring process with clear communication and a compelling narrative about Mistral's mission, culture, and trajectory - Articulate Mistral's positioning in the AI landscape — frontier models, open-weight philosophy, and research credibility — to differentiate us against better-resourced labs - Provide candidates with real insight into our research agenda, compute access, publication culture, and the specific impact of their role - Deliver a high-quality, respectful candidate experience at every stage, regardless of outcome Recruiting Operations & Data-Driven Improvement - Develop and refine technical recruiting processes, tools, and documentation to improve outcomes and efficiency - Use data to diagnose pipeline issues (e.g., drop-off at specific stages, time-to-fill by role) and propose targeted solutions - Build and maintain market maps, competitive intel, and talent pools for key US research and engineering segments - Standardize technical interview rubrics, scorecards, and debrief practices across US technical hiring teams Raising the Bar - Partner on employer-brand and outbound sourcing initiatives — including academic pipelines, conference presence, and open-source community engagement — that position Mistral as a destination for top research and engineering talent What We're Looking For - 6+ years of recruiting experience, including 2+ years in a startup or high-growth environment, with a focus on Research Science and Research Engineering roles - Demonstrated ability to independently hire across the technical stack — from Research Engineers to Research Scientists, and senior research talent - Deep network and sourcing expertise in US research and engineering talent markets, with credibility in AI/ML and ideally connections across top labs and universities - Track record of hiring in competitive, candidate-scarce markets where top researchers have multiple offers - Experience working across multiple US markets, including relocation and visa-driven hiring - Willingness to work on other roles as needs come up - Comfort navigating ambiguity and switching between strategic planning and hands-on execution - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence peers and senior technical stakeholders without direct authority - Organized, detail-oriented, and able to juggle shifting priorities across a high-volume hiring slate - Professional experience with modern recruiting tools such as Ashby - Familiarity with the AI/ML research landscape and the ability to credibly discuss frontier model capabilities, research directions, and publications with technical candidates WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. items.title: International Marketing Lead, SMB Ads
items.description: About the Team OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways. The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth. About the Role We are hiring an International Marketing Lead, SMB Ads, reporting to the Head of SMB Ads Marketing, to build and scale OpenAI’s SMB Ads business outside the United States. You will own SMB business targets across international markets and lead the team and cross-functional plans that deliver advertiser acquisition, activation, retention, and revenue growth. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role at the intersection of product marketing, growth marketing, demand generation, lifecycle marketing, partnerships, and sales enablement. You will directly manage the international SMB Ads marketing team and lead its work within a global matrix: set country priorities and resource choices, translate global strategy and capabilities into regional and local execution, and bring local insight back to shape global plans. In this role, you will: - Own international advertiser and revenue targets. Translate them into country plans spanning acquisition, activation, retention, expansion, and advocacy. - Prioritize countries based on market potential, product readiness, channel economics, and regulatory and operational requirements. Balance global consistency with local relevance. - Launch locally relevant go-to-market programs with regional marketing, sales, and partnership leaders across positioning, demand generation, lifecycle, education, offers, and conversion. - Improve the international advertiser experience with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Operations, from signup and campaign creation to payments, measurement, support, and trust. - Align regional sales leaders around shared growth goals, market plans, enablement, and coordinated customer engagement. - Direct investment across markets and programs. Align budgets, team capacity, agency resources, and global capabilities with growth opportunities, and refine allocation as results emerge. - Lead international performance reviews, forecasting, and growth initiatives with Sales, Product, and Finance. Use experimentation, funnel insights, and return on investment to improve results. - Hire, coach, and develop the international SMB Ads marketing team. Establish clear goals and a culture of experimentation, collaboration, and accountability. - Connect regional and local insights to global strategy. Establish planning and review rhythms that shape marketing, product, and operational roadmaps. You might thrive in this role if you: - Bring significant experience owning international business or growth targets, with measurable customer and revenue results in SMB, self-serve, advertising, SaaS, marketplace, commerce, or fintech businesses. - Demonstrate success hiring and developing marketing teams, scaling across countries, and leading collaboration among global, regional, and local teams. - Balance global strategy with local customer needs, prioritizing investment across markets, segments, and programs. - Understand how to acquire, activate, educate, and retain SMB customers at scale. - Use funnel data, market research, customer insight, and experiments to make clear decisions in evolving markets. - Build trusted partnerships with regional sales and marketing leaders, global specialist teams, Product, Engineering, Partnerships, Legal, and Operations. - Combine growth, lifecycle, content, partner, and field programs into effective market plans. - Bring familiarity with advertiser acquisition, campaign setup, and education on platforms such as Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok for Business, Amazon Ads, Reddit, or Snap. - Translate strategy into execution, launching programs, evaluating results, and scaling successful approaches. items.title: Social Media Manager, Community
items.location_text: Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. We are looking for a Social Media Manager, Community to act as the human extension of our brand across our key social platforms. This is a full-time, senior role for an experienced community professional who will bring a strategic point of view to how Robinhood shows up in social communities. You will balance an accessible, bold, and relatable brand voice with the rigorous compliance standards required in the financial services industry. This role owns community management, social-first storytelling and marketing support — it does not include responding to customer support inquiries on social, which is owned by our dedicated Social CX team. This role is equal parts community builder, listener, writer, and judgment call. You’ll know when to engage, when to elevate feedback, and when precision matters most. This role is based in our New York, NY, and Menlo Park, CA offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Own our community management strategy: Serve as the in-house expert on community management — setting the strategy, tone, and playbooks for how Robinhood shows up across X, Reddit, TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram, and evolving that strategy as platforms, culture, and our audience shift. Own daily community operations: Manage day-to-day community engagement across X, Reddit, TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram — writing social posts, responses, moderating conversations, and keeping our audience active and connected. Speak the language of retail investors: Leverage a deep understanding of online finance communities—especially the unique culture, humor, and rapid pace of finance communities on social—to authentically engage with our audience. Act as the voice of the customer: Monitor overarching community sentiment, utilize social listening tools, and gather real-time feedback to deliver actionable insights to our product and marketing teams. Spearhead community activations: Ideate and execute community-first events, such as live AMAs, platform-specific Q&As, and surprise-and-delight moments for our most dedicated users. Bring a human, community voice to product marketing: Partner with Product Marketing on launches and campaigns for products that call for an authentic, human perspective — shaping social-native creative and messaging, pressure-testing concepts against how our community actually talks, and showing up as the credible, on-the-ground voice of the community throughout the campaign. Stay close to internet culture: Constantly monitor the algorithm, related trends and meme formats, FinTwit narratives, and rising stars to keep Robinhood’s community presence cutting-edge and highly relevant. Represent the Robinhood voice with strong judgment Act as a critical line of defense to ensure all community communications adhere to Robinhood’s Content Standards and strict financial regulations, ensuring information is always fair, balanced, and truthful. What you bring 5+ years of experience in social media or community management, preferably at a fast-paced consumer tech, fintech, or culturally relevant brand, with a track record of owning a channel or program end-to-end. Experience partnering with product marketing, brand, or campaign teams — you know how to translate a product story into content and moments that feel native and human on social, without losing the community voice. A native understanding of platform nuances (especially our priority channels: X TikTok, Reddit, and Instagram) and how different communities operate within them. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; you can seamlessly code-switch between drafting a formal legal brief for compliance and writing culturally relevant posts on X. Data-driven mindset with the ability to translate social metrics (sentiment, engagement rate, conversions) into actionable strategy. Ability to thrive in a highly regulated industry, balancing creative marketing with strict compliance and legal guardrails. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $128,000 — $150,000 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $112,000 — $132,000 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $99,000 — $117,000 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

items.description: Fireblocks is the company bringing global finance onchain. Backed by over $1 billion in capital, we are the premier digital asset infrastructure provider trusted by thousands of industry-defining financial institutions, including banks, payment providers, fintechs, and global corporates such as BNY Mellon, BNP Paribas, ANZ Bank, Western Union, Stripe, and Revolut. Built for institutional scale and security, our enterprise-grade platform and network have powered over $14 trillion in digital asset transfers worldwide. Fireblocks is looking for a Global Total Rewards Lead to lead our compensation and benefits programs across every market we operate in. You'll be the subject-matter expert on global comp benchmarking and benefits, and the operational owner of our two annual review cycles: the full annual compensation review and a mid-year mini cycle. This is a hands-on, high-visibility role for someone who loves both the strategic and technical sides of Total Rewards - building comp philosophy and structures, while also being deeply fluent in the tools that power them. You'll work closely with People Operations, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and business leaders globally to ensure Fireblocks pays competitively, fairly, and in a way that supports our growth as a global tech company. What You'll Do Own the annual and mid-year review cycles end-to-end - timeline execution, calibration, budget modeling, manager enablement, communications, and post-cycle reporting for both the full annual comp review and the mid-year mini cycle. Manage global compensation architecture , including job leveling, global salary bands/ranges, market pricing, and pay equity analysis across all regions where Fireblocks operates. Serve as the internal expert on Radford , using it for market data benchmarking, offer/band validation, and comp analytics that inform both cycles and day-to-day hiring decisions. Serve as the internal expert on HiBob & Pave , managing comp and benefits workflows, data integrity, reporting, and cycle configuration within the HRIS. Design and manage global benefits programs , balancing consistency with local market competitiveness and statutory requirements across multiple countries. Partner with Talent Acquisition on offer approvals, competitive positioning, and market intelligence to support hiring in a competitive tech talent market. Partner with Finance on comp budgeting, forecasting, and headcount cost modeling tied to both review cycles. Build manager and employee-facing communications to ensure transparency and understanding of comp decisions and total rewards philosophy. Monitor pay equity and compliance across jurisdictions, staying current on evolving pay transparency legislation globally. Continuously benchmark and refine Fireblocks' total rewards philosophy to keep it competitive with the broader tech and fintech markets. items.title: Total Rewards Lead
items.description: Fireblocks is the company bringing global finance onchain. Backed by over $1 billion in capital, we are the premier digital asset infrastructure provider trusted by thousands of industry-defining financial institutions, including banks, payment providers, fintechs, and global corporates such as BNY Mellon, BNP Paribas, ANZ Bank, Western Union, Stripe, and Revolut. Built for institutional scale and security, our enterprise-grade platform and network have powered over $14 trillion in digital asset transfers worldwide. Fireblocks is looking for a Global Total Rewards Lead to lead our compensation and benefits programs across every market we operate in. You'll be the subject-matter expert on global comp benchmarking and benefits, and the operational owner of our two annual review cycles: the full annual compensation review and a mid-year mini cycle. This is a hands-on, high-visibility role for someone who loves both the strategic and technical sides of Total Rewards - building comp philosophy and structures, while also being deeply fluent in the tools that power them. You'll work closely with People Operations, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and business leaders globally to ensure Fireblocks pays competitively, fairly, and in a way that supports our growth as a global tech company. What You'll Do Own the annual and mid-year review cycles end-to-end - timeline execution, calibration, budget modeling, manager enablement, communications, and post-cycle reporting for both the full annual comp review and the mid-year mini cycle. Manage global compensation architecture , including job leveling, global salary bands/ranges, market pricing, and pay equity analysis across all regions where Fireblocks operates. Serve as the internal expert on Radford , using it for market data benchmarking, offer/band validation, and comp analytics that inform both cycles and day-to-day hiring decisions. Serve as the internal expert on HiBob & Pave , managing comp and benefits workflows, data integrity, reporting, and cycle configuration within the HRIS. Design and manage global benefits programs , balancing consistency with local market competitiveness and statutory requirements across multiple countries. Partner with Talent Acquisition on offer approvals, competitive positioning, and market intelligence to support hiring in a competitive tech talent market. Partner with Finance on comp budgeting, forecasting, and headcount cost modeling tied to both review cycles. Build manager and employee-facing communications to ensure transparency and understanding of comp decisions and total rewards philosophy. Monitor pay equity and compliance across jurisdictions, staying current on evolving pay transparency legislation globally. Continuously benchmark and refine Fireblocks' total rewards philosophy to keep it competitive with the broader tech and fintech markets. What We're Looking For 5+ years of experience in Total Rewards / Compensation & Benefits , with direct ownership of full-cycle annual comp review. Must have tech industry experience - you understand tech company pay structures, equity compensation, and the competitive dynamics of hiring in tech. We build and run programs that create pipeline, accelerate opportunities, deepen executive relationships, and bring OpenAI’s latest innovations directly to enterprise decision-makers. About the Role As an Enterprise Field Marketer, you will be a growth partner to Enterprise Sales, owning field marketing programs that create pipeline, accelerate strategic opportunities, and deepen relationships with priority enterprise accounts. Your focus will attach to the business’s most important needs at any given time, whether that means an industry motion, a regional priority, a strategic account, an executive engagement, or a new company-wide growth opportunity. You will own the full program lifecycle: translating sales priorities into field plans, identifying the right accounts and moments, executing high-quality customer programs, driving follow-up with sellers, and measuring business impact. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE Mistral AI is seeking Applied Scientist Interns and Research Engineer Interns based in Korea to join our team for six months in Paris or London, and then help build our new Seoul office as full-time team members. You will develop SOTA models across different modalities such as text, image, and speech. By developing novel methods and research ideas you will apply these models across a diverse set of use cases and domains. Working cross-functionally with both external and internal science, engineering, and product teams you will deliver high-impact AI solutions that turn the needle. Location and Work Authorization This internship is based in Paris or London for 6 months, with visa sponsorship and relocation support provided by Mistral. It is designed as a pathway into our Seoul office: on completion, successful interns will be offered a full-time role in Seoul. Candidates must be based in Korea and eligible to work there after the internship. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Run pre-training, post-training and deploy state of the art models on clusters with thousands of GPUs. - Generate and curate data for pre-training and post-training, working on evaluations and making sure the model's performance beats expectations. - Develop the necessary tools and frameworks to facilitate data generation, model training, evaluation and deployment. - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to tackle complex use cases using agents and retrieval pipelines. - Manage research projects and communications with client research teams. NICE TO HAVE - Pursuing a PhD / Master in a relevant field (Mathematics, Physics, Machine Learning) — exceptional candidates from other backgrounds welcome. - Preferred duration: 6 months. Priority to candidates about to finalise their studies. - Research experience in agents, multimodal models, world models, robotics, diffusion models, cybersecurity, 3D understanding/generation, or time-series analysis. - Contributions to a large open-source or industry codebase. - Publications in top academic journals or conferences. - Enjoys improving existing code: typing, tests, CI pipelines. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. items.title: Engineering Manager – Growth Foundations
items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page https://www.kraken.com/culture to understand what drives us and how we work. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. The Growth Foundations team builds the AI-native Growth Engine, enabling Growth teams across the company. We design and ship powerful AI-driven systems, tools and automations, as well as own the core infrastructure of Growth tools such as our website, user communications and martech. It’s a team with direct influence on company growth, global reach, and user engagement at scale. Our products serve millions of users globally. THE ROLE As an Engineering Manager within Growth Foundations, you’ll lead and develop a team of engineers who deliver high-impact features, platforms, and tools that power our growth. You’ll ensure the team is aligned, supported, and set up to execute with excellence — turning complex challenges into simple, reliable solutions that reach users around the world. items.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Financial Services- NYC
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with banks, asset managers, insurers, and private capital firms to deploy production-grade AI systems in high-stakes financial environments. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, embedding deeply with customers to translate frontier model capabilities into reliable, auditable systems that create measurable business impact. Our work turns early deployments into repeatable solution patterns, operating standards, and evaluation practices that scale across regulated financial institutions. ABOUT THE ROLE We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to lead end-to-end deployments of OpenAI’s models inside financial services organizations where correctness, latency, explainability, and control matter. You will work with customers who are experts in investment banking, trading, risk, compliance, underwriting, research, operations, or investment decision-making, translating complex workflows, data constraints, and regulatory requirements into production systems. You will measure success through production adoption, workflow efficiency, risk reduction, revenue impact, and evaluation-driven feedback loops that inform product, model, and GTM strategy. You’ll work closely with Product, Research, GTM, Security, Legal, and GRC to deliver systems that meet enterprise standards for governance, auditability, and operational resilience. You will also play a central role in shaping OpenAI’s Financial Services offering — identifying high-value use cases, defining solution patterns, and building the first repeatable deployments that scale across institutions. Learn more about some of our work with financial institutions https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-financial-services/. This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% may be required. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Design and ship production AI systems around models, owning integrations, data flows, reliability, observability, and on-call readiness across financial workflows. - Lead discovery and scoping from pre-sales through post-production, translating ambiguous business problems into hypothesis-driven problem framing, system requirements, and delivery plans with measurable outcomes. - Define and enforce launch criteria for regulated financial environments, including controls, audit artifacts, evaluation benchmarks, and acceptance thresholds tied to risk and performance. - Build in sensitive data environments where access controls, data lineage, explainability, and failure modes shape architecture and operating procedures. - Run evaluation loops that measure model and system quality against workflow-specific financial benchmarks (e.g., accuracy, latency, coverage, false positives) and use results to drive iteration. - Own delivery state across multiple workstreams, making trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality to protect production outcomes. - Distill deployment learnings into hardened primitives, reference architectures, playbooks, and tooling that scale across financial institutions. - Surface field feedback that informs model behavior, product capabilities, and platform gaps in real-world financial use cases. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Bring 5+ years of software engineering, ML engineering, or technical deployment experience with customer-facing ownership in financial services or adjacent regulated industries. - Have owned complex AI or data-driven systems end-to-end, from scoping through production adoption, in environments where errors carry real financial or regulatory consequences. - Have experience with financial workflows such as research, trading, risk, compliance, underwriting, operations, or investment processes, and understand how incentives and controls shape adoption. - Write and review production-grade code across backend and frontend systems using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks. - Have deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behavior, evaluation, and guardrails affect user trust and business outcomes. - Communicate clearly across engineering, product, risk, compliance, and executive stakeholders, translating technical trade-offs into decision quality and risk posture. - Apply systems thinking with high execution standards, turning incidents, escalations, and failures into improved operating standards and repeatable deployment patterns. - Stay calm and decisive when delivery is urgent, ambiguous, and high-stakes. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.
